brief: Goldman's derivatives desk calls current conditions "as challenging as we have seen" after the S&P fell seven straight sessions and the VIX jumped over 16 points, the fifth-largest weekly VIX spike on record, pushing Goldman's US Vol Panic Index to a record 9.8/10. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief: after the four prior comparable VIX spikes (2008, 2010, Feb 2020, Apr 2025), the S&P rose the next day and the next week every time, fell two weeks out, was flat a month out, then gained an average 26.5% a year out. But each of those four episodes was followed by a policy "blink" (bank recapitalizations, a euro bailout, an emergency Fed cut, a tariff pause), and the Fed is still hiking now. Thin liquidity ($4mm top-of-book, ETFs over 39% of Friday's tape), dealers short gamma, and CTAs net short $19bn after selling $57bn keep the "trapdoor" risk open even as the Nasdaq looks oversold (RSI 26.5). Copper fell over 9% as CTA selling overwhelmed an already-long physical market. Goldman's TMT desk notes cheap valuations (17x Nasdaq, 12-13x semis) but a buyers' strike, with charts already favoring stocks that pre-announced cuts (FFIV, INTC) over fundamentals. Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all hold 2027 S&P targets of 8,700.
